Again, sincerely asking just one (1) JCPOA opponent to stop lying about the sequence of events here.

JCPOA happened. Some people didn’t like it. Proponents said “the realistic alternative to this is war.” Opponents angrily denied that. And now here we are._


Russell Hickson (@RussHickson)

It was not a flip flop, arguments against the JCPOA always included a credible threat to deter Iranian aggression. In 2015 Trump argued the US should not take military options off the table. Trump never rule

How many times are markets going to get whipsawed by meaningless Trump announcements?


First Squawk (@FirstSquawk)

IRANIAN PARLIAMENT: THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ WILL NOT OPEN, WE HAVE NOT HELD ANY NEGOTIATIONS, AND WE WILL NOT HOLD THEM

You not only should help people when you can, you ought to feel fortunate to be able to make a difference and do something worthwhile with your time.

slowboring.com/p/the-real-pr…

There’s nothing wrong with getting rich — if you built up a net worth of billions you probably did something useful.

But spending all that money on high living or your own kids rather than giving some to those in need is genuinely problematic.

slowboring.com/p/the-real-pr…

I think literally zero of them have even acknowledged that this flip flop took place, and they’re now all claiming the military campaign has worked out just as they hoped when that’s clearly not the case either.

I know I’m a little hung up on this but the shameless dishonesty of the Iran Hawks who vociferously denied that their preferred alternative to JCPOA was war only to turn around and insist this war was necessary really bothers me.

As I have written, people are raising their standards, and only couple up when it's more rewarding than alternatives. 

So those with a less attractive package get ghosted and ignored.

Werner Zagrebbi🇦🇿 (@zagrebbi)

I added a Jewish estimate to the "what if Columbia admissions used only the SAT" simulation. 
Contra Ron Unz — who famously argued Jews are overrepresented at elite schools relative to merit — Jews at Columbia would actually be more represented under pure test-score selection, not less: 6.5% of top scorers vs. 5.4% of the actual class.
